# sfcompute_order (Resource)

Manages an SF Compute order (created with `POST /v2/orders`; it cannot be updated in place, so any change replaces it).

~> **Spends money.** Creating this resource is blocked unless the provider is configured with `allow_spending = true`, because it places a buy or sell order on the SF Compute market, which can spend credits (or sell your compute) as soon as it fills.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Requires allow_spending = true in the provider block. This places a real
# order on the SF Compute market; credits are spent as soon as it fills.
# Destroying the resource cancels whatever has not filled yet.
resource "sfcompute_pool" "dev" {
  name = "dev"
}

resource "sfcompute_order" "two_hours" {
  pool                              = sfcompute_pool.dev.id
  side                              = "buy"
  sku                               = "sku_4UpxzQw7A8N"
  allow_standing                    = true
  allow_partial                     = false
  limit_price_dollars_per_node_hour = "20.00"
  allocation_schedule_delta = [
    # Unix timestamps on the allocation schedule grid
    # (see data source sfcompute_platform_constants).
    { start_at = 1767225600, end_at = 1767232800, node_count = 1 },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `allocation_schedule_delta` (Attributes List) Change in capacity if the order fills (added on `buy`, subtracted on `sell`). Must be a single time range: one `node_count` held constant from `start_at` to `end_at`, with both set. `start_at` and `end_at` are Unix timestamps in seconds on the [allocation schedule grid](https://docs.sfcompute.com/api-reference/platform/get-platform-constants#response-allocation-schedule-grid); `start_at` can also be the current time. `node_count` must be between 1 and 10000. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--allocation_schedule_delta))
- `allow_partial` (Boolean) If true, the order may fill partially — fewer nodes and/or a subset of the requested time window. The filled time may be disjoint.
- `allow_standing` (Boolean) If true, the order rests on the order book until it fills, is cancelled, or its end time passes. If false, the order is cancelled immediately if it does not fill.
- `limit_price_dollars_per_node_hour` (String) Price in dollars per node-hour, encoded as a decimal string. Prices are rounded to the nearest $0.000060/node-hour market tick. This is one microdollar per node-minute. Responses contain the rounded value with six decimal places. Inputs must contain a decimal point, be non-negative, and not exceed $500/node-hour.
- `pool` (String) Target pool that receives compute when filled.
- `side` (String)
- `sku` (String) SKU this order will fill on. Rejected at submission if the SKU id is not registered. Any id spelling is accepted.

### Optional

- `_preview_preemption_limit_price_multiple` (String) **Preview.** Buy orders only. SF Compute lists the compute this order fills for sale at `limit_price_dollars_per_node_hour` times this multiple, rounded up to the next $0.000060/node-hour, as standing sell orders on the same pool that allow partial fills. Must be greater than `"1.0"` and at most `"1.5"`.

When a listing fills, the pool loses that time and its instances terminate, lowest priority first. Sell fees apply. Cancelling this order doesn't cancel its listings.

The order doesn't count toward your compute limit.

### Read-Only

- `cancelled_at` (Number) Unix timestamp.
- `created_at` (Number) Unix timestamp.
- `filled_allocation_schedule_delta` (Attributes List) The total portion of the requested schedule that has filled. Once `state` is `cancelled`, this is final and remains available on later get and list responses. Empty for orders with no fills; the unfilled remainder is `allocation_schedule_delta` minus this. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--filled_allocation_schedule_delta))
- `filled_at` (Number) Unix timestamp.
- `fills` (Attributes List) Complete list of contracts produced by this order. Once `state` is `cancelled`, this list is final and remains available on later get and list responses. Omitted for orders with no fills. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--fills))
- `id` (String) Order ID
- `state` (String) Current state of the order.
- `workspace` (Attributes) Workspace that owns the order's pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--workspace))

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sfcompute_order.two_hours ordr_hYuOEmXWt3RqPd8KvA2Nc
```
